beats.text: He banked America's blood. Then they segregated it.

overlays.hook: He banked America's blood. *Then they segregated it.*

beats.text: In 1940, he earned a doctorate at Columbia, with a study on how to store blood. He was the first African American to earn one there.
That year, Britain was at war and short of blood. Drew ran the Blood for Britain project.
Nearly fifteen thousand people gave blood, and the plasma was shipped across the ocean.

visual.caption: American Red Cross Blood Donor Service poster, 1940s

beats.text: In 1941, he became director of the first American Red Cross Blood Bank.

visual.caption: Drew's letter to the Red Cross, 1941

beats.text: He set up trucks to collect blood, the idea later known as bloodmobiles.

visual.caption: Red Cross blood donor cars, Syracuse, New York, 1943

beats.text: Then came the rule. Blood from Black donors had to be kept separate.
There was no scientific reason for it. Blood is blood.
He went back to Howard University to teach surgery.

visual.caption: Dr. Charles R. Drew with young doctors, about 1945

beats.text: He died after a car crash in 1950. He was forty-five.
And the story that a white hospital refused to treat him? Historians call it a myth.

visual.title: Myth
visual.sub: He was treated. His injuries were too severe.

beats.text: He built the blood bank, and he would not accept its color line.

facts.claim: Columbia doctorate 1940, thesis Banked Blood; first African American to earn it there.
Medical director of Blood for Britain, New York, 1940.
Nearly 15,000 donors (WIKI) / over 14,500 donations, plasma shipped to Britain (NARA).
Director of the first (WIKI) / new (NARA) American Red Cross Blood Bank, 1941.
Developed collection trucks later known as bloodmobiles.
Blood of Black donors kept separate (Red Cross announced segregation Jan 1942).
No scientific basis for segregating blood.
Returned to Howard University / Freedmen's Hospital as surgeon and professor.
Died after a car crash near Burlington, NC, 1950, aged 45.
Story that a white hospital refused him is a myth; injuries too severe.

notUsed: Exact plasma volume (5,000 liters only in NARA; Wikipedia gives 5,500 vials).
Bloodmobile stated as his invention outright: worded as "later known as bloodmobiles".
